quests.region: Bemidji logging trail and a forgotten northern camp
quests.stage: optional late campaign; access clues before the League
quests.premise: A retired trail worker asks why an abandoned skid road is filling with water despite clear culverts. The huge hoofprints and neatly stacked windthrow suggest two creatures repairing damage differently.
steps: Read the trail worker's account and inspect the dry culvert, crescent hoofprint pool, and windthrow stack. Each clue changes the worker's next response.

At the forgotten camp, trace the old drainage ditch to a low crossing. Reopen the existing footpath without cutting live trees. Bunjant first appears across the ditch, watches, then leaves a marked log.
Return the marked-log observation to the worker. Their old tally describes the same crescent prints before the camp existed; this is a tall tale, not evidence of a historical giant.
Follow the newly readable hoofprint sequence to Babehemoth's pool. Its optional encounter becomes available independently of capturing Bunjant.
Return to the camp after the footpath is acknowledged safe. Bunjant's optional encounter becomes available independently of capturing Babehemoth.
quests.discovery_distinction: Babehemoth follows landscape-scale tracks and pooled water; Bunjant responds to how the player restores a damaged work site. The two reveals are separate and neither capture gates the other.
quests.completion: Worker acknowledges the safe path and the two distinct signs, regardless of battle outcomes.

quests.region: Lake Pepin; preserve the existing main river and fishing quest
quests.premise: A dock observer has three sketches of a wake that travels against the wind. A working boat operator thinks it is a submerged snag until the player compares the sightings.
steps: Read the dock sketch: a wake crosses the current, then turns upstream after the boat has passed. Do not add buoy or marker props.
Observe a shoreline eddy from land and a sheltered reed opening from Surf. These are distinct acknowledged viewpoints, not three copies of one sign.
Compare all three observations at the dock. The operator identifies a safe sheltered inlet and explains how to approach without entering the shipping channel.
Follow the optional inlet loop to the still pool. Pepivern surfaces with paddlewheel fins; the player may watch and leave or accept the encounter.
quests.discovery_distinction: The clue is the direction and shape of the wake, not a rare fishing roll or a forced whirlpool gate.
quests.completion: The dock record gains the matched three-wake account even if the player declines battle.
quests.presentation_contract: Use existing native shoreline, water and ordinary dock actors. No custom signs, tables, campfires or buoy props. Land and Surf viewpoints must be reachable through the actual current geometry.

quests.region: State Fair exhibit and its ordinary service return
quests.stage: optional after the fair opens; no paid admission dependency
quests.premise: An exhibit attendant admits the label was written to sell tickets. Three witnesses disagree about the silhouette inside the ice. The mystery concerns the creature and unreliable recollection, not a claim that the sideshow legend is fact.
steps: Speak to the attendant, a delivery worker and a visitor. Each describes a different face; the player can read their short accounts in any order.
Inspect the intact rear latch and the meltwater tray. Neither supports the attendant's story that somebody replaced the specimen.
Return after those accounts are acknowledged. The attendant takes down the invented label and asks for help moving the warming case into shade.
Use the ordinary service passage and compare the empty case with a second patch of cloudy ice. The silhouette has moved on its own. Icemyth offers a voluntary encounter there.
quests.discovery_distinction: Contradictory witness pages and the physical case lead to an honest corrected label; no real-time day, external event code or irreversible wrong-answer lock.
quests.completion: The exhibit keeps the corrected account and stops advertising a certainty it cannot support.

quests.region: Big Bog-inspired northwest spur from Bemidji/Border Pines
quests.premise: A walker felt something shift under one boot. A worn root, a small pool and the moss on a peat ridge move in sequence and uncover an old crossing into a northern hollow.
steps: Find the worn root on the west side, the notch in the pool south of it, and the hanging moss on the east ridge. The three observations can be made in any order.
The last observation shows the root, pool and moss moving in turn. A player who already recorded all three can also compare them with the observer.
Revisit the same landmarks in root, pool, moss order. The nearby original contacts still work. A mistaken or repeated touch points to the next feature and retains completed steps.
Lifting the moss opens the path to the northern hollow. The original dry path leads back to Bemidji Northwoods. The current Minnesota encounter here is MITWIST.
quests.discovery_distinction: Layer order and repeated geography replace a real-time clock requirement. No invention that Waskish is already on R17; site connection must respect the accepted map.
quests.completion: The three observations reveal the sequence. The encounter and its outcome leave the open path available.

quests.region: Agassiz beach-ridge prairie between Detroit Lakes and Moorhead; fictional optional basin chamber
quests.premise: A basin surveyor asks the player to compare three ridges left by different lake levels. Strandrak's crescent shell carries the same nested pattern.
steps: Walk each of three ridge terraces and read their distinct shoreline marks from high to low. Their ordinary returns remain accessible before and after solving the puzzle.
Compare the marks at the survey shelter. The surveyor separates observed beach ridges from the fictional guardian story.
Inside the optional basin, set three outlet indicators to their corresponding former levels. Wrong settings leave the exit open and give local feedback; the player can inspect clues again.
A small inner basin drains while the outside route remains unchanged. Strandrak braces the outlet with its forked forearms and becomes available for a voluntary encounter.
quests.discovery_distinction: Three nested terraces and an intelligible outlet mechanism, not a warp maze with arbitrary combinations. No draining of real regional waters or main-route obstruction.
quests.completion: The basin survey is complete before the encounter choice; all ordinary travel stays open.

quests.region: Red River Prairie field-margin spur on R16; a moving-stone mystery inspired by Kensington boundary-marker stories
quests.premise: A caretaker finds stone markers turning toward a buried field boundary. The mystery is the movement of an original creature, not proof of medieval settlement.
steps: Read the caretaker's account and compare three markers: fresh soil on the reverse, a matching buried edge, and grooves that change between inspections.
Follow the field margin rather than crossing the crop rows. Locate the displaced boundary marker and return its location to the caretaker.
The caretaker withdraws a historical claim from the account he keeps and records what was actually observed.
Return along the margin. Kensigard has risen from the buried edge and now faces the restored boundary. The player can approach voluntarily.
quests.discovery_distinction: Observation, a clear crop-respecting loop, and a corrected claim; no fictional archaeological proof or item fetched from a different legendary quest.
quests.completion: The caretaker acknowledges the located boundary and corrected notice before capture is possible.
